# Dense ITK HDF5 group fixtures

`mixed.h5` was written and read by the public SimpleITK 2.5.6 API on Windows
amd64 with Python 3.12, ITK 5.4 and its HDF5 1.12.1 writer. The synthetic
composite has 58 components, including an oblique displacement field,
a cubic B-spline, an affine and translations. The writer used both a
v2 internal B-tree node and an indirect fractal heap block for the group.
The Go test checks the reversed application order, physical LPS points in
millimetres, and position Jacobians at three interior points and one
outside point. The Jacobian reference comes from public ITK point evaluations
with centered differences at a step of 1/65536 mm.

`ordered.h5` was written and read by h5py 3.16.0/HDF5 2.0.0 with v1.8
layout bounds. Its 73 hard links exercise both a name index and a creation
order index with internal nodes. A second dense group contains a soft link
to verify explicit refusal. The fixture manifest records the SHA-256 of
both files and the independently read link order. The earlier
[`itkhdf5`](../itkhdf5/README.md) and [`itk1345`](../itk1345/README.md)
fixtures cover the single-block dense heap, compact and symbol-table
groups, and linear transforms written by ITK.

Generate these synthetic files with the public APIs using
`py -3.12 generate.py <output-directory>`. The files contain no patient data.
Version and HDF5 metadata may change the generated bytes and their hashes.
The committed reference files and manifest run without Python.

The reader profile admits 7-byte IDs for managed objects in unfiltered
version 0 fractal heaps. It accepts version 0 v2 B-tree name and optional
creation-order indexes, and reads direct and indirect blocks. Each heap has
a 16 MiB budget for read blocks including metadata. Each dense index is
bounded to 65,536 records and nodes, 32 levels below the root and 1 MiB per
node. The transform reader separately limits files to 1,024 records
including the composite marker and enforces its decoded parameter budget.
The indexes, heap blocks and link records must agree. Repeated nodes,
overlapping objects, invalid checksums and cyclic paths fail explicitly.

Filtered heaps, huge and tiny heap IDs, dense non-hard links and newer
dataset chunk indexes remain outside the profile. Dense-group support
changes reading. The writer continues to produce classic symbol tables.
[HDF5 File Format Specification 3.0](https://docs.hdfgroup.org/documentation/hdf5/latest/_f_m_t3.html)
